title: Testing: TestBed, harnesses and what belongs at each level

videos.script:
The planner has had test files since lesson two, but most of them only check that a class can be made. This lesson writes tests that say something, at every level Angular has.

{{runner}} First, what runs them. Vitest, in Node, with a pretend DOM called jsdom, and no browser at all.

{{functions}} Then the planner's arithmetic, tested by calling it. Then a deliberate mistake, to prove that the tests would notice one.

{{server}} The store is tested against a fake server. The test answers every request itself, including the refusal that is hard to cause by hand.

{{components}} A component is tested through the page it draws. The test reads the rows a person would read, not the fields of the class.

{{harnesses}} For Material's checkbox, the test uses a harness. It works the control by what it says, without knowing how Material builds it.

{{karma}} Most Angular code you meet at work was tested with Karma and Jasmine. One schematic moves a test across, and the lesson reads what it changed.

{{levels}} Last, what belongs at each level. Each rule goes to the cheapest test that can see it.
